cards.text: Jesus leaves that place and heads into the region of Judea, beyond the Jordan. And here come the crowds, AGAIN. Friend, I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS and couldn't get one visitor, and this Man can't cross a river without a crowd finding Him.

cards.question: The crowds gather around Jesus in Judea. What does He do with them, the way He always does?

cards.text: Then some Pharisees walk up, from the strictest group in the Jewish religion (Acts 26:5). And Mark doesn't hide it: they came to test Him.

cards.question: The Pharisees came to test Jesus. What do they ask Him?

answers.text: Whether it's lawful for a man to divorce his wife
Whether it's lawful to pay taxes to Caesar
Whether it's lawful to heal on the Sabbath

cards.text: They hand Jesus a test, and He hands one RIGHT back. Like when a coworker tries to catch you in a meeting and you go, "Great question. What does the handbook say?"

cards.question: Jesus answers the Pharisees with a question of His own: What did ___ command you?

cards.text: The Pharisees came READY, like they had the page bookmarked. They go straight to what Moses, Israel's lawgiver, wrote in the law (Deuteronomy 24:1).

cards.question: What do the Pharisees say Moses permitted a man to write his wife before sending her away?

cards.text: Jesus calls it a commandment Moses wrote for them. Then He tells them WHY Moses wrote it.

cards.question: Why does Jesus say Moses wrote the commandment about the certificate of divorce?

answers.text: Because of their hardness of heart
Because a famine had struck the land
Because their elders had asked him to

cards.text: Then Jesus goes WAY back, past Moses, all the way to the beginning of creation. And here I thought I was old-school every time I start a story with "Back in the drawer…"

cards.question: Jesus goes back to the beginning of creation. What does He say God made them?

cards.text: Then Jesus quotes Genesis again (Genesis 2:24). A man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says that once a man and his wife are united, they stay two separate people.
Jesus draws His conclusion for the Pharisees. Who does He say joins a husband and wife together?
Jesus tells the Pharisees that what God has joined together, let man not ___.

cards.text: Later, they're back inside the house, and the subject comes up again. Every kitchen I've ever known works like that: company leaves, and THEN the real questions come out.

cards.question: True or false: back inside the house, the Pharisees ask Jesus more about divorce.
Jesus tells His disciples that whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits ___ against her.
True or false: Jesus says the same goes for a woman. If she divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 11 quotes "Back in the drawer", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin 'couldn't get one visitor' in the junk drawer. That contradicts his backstory. Newcomers like the can opener slid into the drawer, he welcomed every one of them, and the angel came to the drawer.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'They hand Jesus a test, and He hands one RIGHT back' says Jesus asked His question as a test. The text says only that the Pharisees came to test Him (Mark 10:2). It gives no purpose for Jesus' reply, 'What did Moses command you?' (Mark 10:3).

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: 'Then Jesus quotes Genesis again' depends on an earlier Genesis quote that no card identified. Card 11 and card 12 never say that 'God made them male and female' comes from Genesis, and that quote never gets its reference (Genesis 1:27).

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: No card ever tells the heart of Mark 10:8: 'the two will become one flesh.' Card 13 stops at verse 7. Card 14 only asks whether the couple stays two separate people. The baker can leave Prep without hearing 'one flesh,' the key phrase of Jesus' answer.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The setup joke 'company leaves, and THEN the real questions come out' tells the baker that the visitors are gone before anyone asks. That gives away the answer to card 18's true or false question about whether the Pharisees ask Jesus more back inside the house.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
